Organic: Biochemical mechanisms and regulation of vitamins and vitamin-like cofactors


RAR/RXR signaling becomes increasingly important in aging due in part to vitamin-related regulatory functions related to
inﬂammation, immunity, and protection of the neural system. Based on studies in knockout mice, vitamin A-related developmental
pathologies are compounded when more than one of the RAR genes is inactivated. Although few congenital structural disabilities
have been reported due to vitamin A deﬁciency, RAR genes are nevertheless essential for organogenesis and early mammalian devel-
opment. As a ﬁnal comment, in addition to transcriptional regulation, RARs and RXRs have nongenomic functions. RARs interact
with several protein kinases systems whose signaling cascades are initiated by receptors at the cell surface.
